docs.title: NameMCSniper
docs.text: NameMCSniper schedules Minecraft Java Edition profile name changes. The Rust build opens a guided terminal menu for checking accounts, previewing a schedule, and confirming a live rename.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Open the Rust executable. On Windows, double-click namemcsniper.exe. Installation
  2. Choose 3 · Try an offline simulation to see how a result looks.
  3. Choose 2 · Check my Minecraft account for one bearer token, or 7 · Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt) for a file. Authentication
  4. Choose 1 · Schedule a name change. Enter the target, pick a time, and review the account and schedule before you confirm. Schedule a rename

For three-character names, the menu can pull the estimated release window from 3NAME. You can also enter a specific time. Sniping tips

docs.title: Why I switched from Python to Rust
docs.text:
I wanted NameMCSniper to open from Explorer and give me more control over when a rename request leaves the app. The Rust build produces a native executable. I moved request preparation ahead of the drop and used a monotonic timer for the final wait. The app rechecks UTC if it detects a change to the system clock.

The rewrite also checks rename eligibility before dispatch, keeps a verified UTC correction through brief outages, and reports results for each account in a group. The offline benchmark measures local dispatch delay. The drop estimate, network path, and Minecraft's response determine what happens after that. How it works

docs.title: Using these docs
docs.text:
These pages cover the Rust checkout and its builds. The public GitHub release still contains the Python edition. Python v3.0.0 release

  • Local files and settings covers tokens.txt, proxies.txt, and run logs.
  • Command reference covers the terminal commands and flags.
  • Troubleshooting covers missed times, token errors, and rate limits.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: NameMCSniper schedules a rename on an existing Minecraft Java Edition profile. The menu lets you review a schedule before choosing an account. A guided live run requires you to type RENAME after reviewing the name, time, and selected profiles. From a shell, snipe --live requires a profile UUID or a token file. simulate and benchmark use scripted responses offline. Command reference

docs.title: Resolve the scheduled time
docs.text: For a three-character username, NameMCSniper can look up the bounds published by 3NAME. A “Dropping Now” listing can have only a latest bound. The menu offers each future bound as a separate choice. Manual times use RFC 3339 with an explicit offset or Unix milliseconds. The two-minute shortcut counts elapsed time from when you select it. Its displayed UTC time uses the system clock at selection. 3NAME · Schedule options

docs.title: Verify UTC and wait
docs.text:
For an absolute live schedule, NameMCSniper queries Cloudflare, Windows Time, and NIST in parallel using NTP. It requires at least two accepted sources whose offsets agree within 50 ms. The app applies the correction to its own UTC estimate and uses a monotonic clock to track elapsed time toward the scheduled slot. Corrections are capped at five minutes. NTP offset and filtering

During a long wait before the account check, the app refreshes the correction roughly every two minutes. It also checks again if it detects a clock jump or the countdown wakes unexpectedly late. After a transient refresh failure, it can continue with the last verified correction while the oldest selected sample is under ten minutes old and estimated uncertainty stays at or below 350 ms. If UTC verification fails outside those limits, the absolute schedule stops. Clock troubleshooting

docs.title: Verify the profiles and prepare the request
docs.text:
The app checks that each token belongs to the selected Java profile UUID and that the profile can rename. It schedules these checks 20 seconds before the first slot for one to four profiles and starts earlier for larger groups, up to 2 minutes 45 seconds before the slot for 64 profiles. The budget covers two phases of up to four concurrent reads, a five-second timeout per read, and five seconds of margin. If less time remains, checks start as soon as possible.

The app prepares the rename request ahead of dispatch and reuses the HTTP client from the account checks. In group mode, it can skip an ineligible profile if another remains. Preflight aborts on HTTP 429 or a profile UUID mismatch. Authentication

docs.title: Dispatch the rename
docs.text:
The only write is PUT /minecraft/profile/name/{name} to Minecraft Services. The guided menu schedules one slot. A script with exactly one --account UUID can schedule up to three slots, at least 10 seconds apart. Only a confirmed unavailable result advances to a later slot. Each slot has one second of scheduling grace before the app skips it. A group run uses one slot and sends one concurrent request per ready profile. The token file can contain up to 64 entries. MCsniperGO's rename request · Command reference

NameMCSniper confirms a rename when the response identifies both the target name and the authorized profile UUID. If a reply leaves the outcome unclear, the app can read the profile back once to verify the result. HTTP 429 ends the schedule after any requests already in progress, and a rate-limited batch skips follow-up profile reads. If the outcome is still uncertain or you cancel during the request, check the selected profile before sending another rename. Live outcome troubleshooting

docs.title: Inspect the results
docs.text:
The terminal displays the outcome for each attempt and, in a group run, for each profile. The live run prints its log path. The log records the schedule, clock checks, dispatch times, and results. It excludes bearer tokens and proxy credentials. The default directory on Windows is %LOCALAPPDATA%\NameMCSniper\logs. Log locations

The proxy checker makes a separate, unauthenticated HTTPS request through each proxy. Live renames use a direct connection to Minecraft Services. Proxy setup

docs.title: Choose a time you can verify
docs.text:
Start with 1 · Schedule a name change. For a three-character name, the menu shows any future bounds from 3NAME. You can inspect the same estimate with namemcsniper drop NAME. Look at both timestamps and how far apart they are. The name may still be unavailable at the earliest bound, and another player may claim it before the latest bound. If the bounds are hours apart, check for an updated estimate closer to the drop or use a time you have independently verified. 3NAME · MCsniperGO's notes on drop windows

The automatic command-line schedule accepts a 3NAME window up to 30 seconds wide. The same limit applies to a manual range made with --at and --until. A single attempt over an accepted range is scheduled for its latest bound. In the menu, you can select an individual future bound or enter a time with an explicit UTC offset. Review the UTC time in the preview before continuing. Schedule options

docs.title: Check the clock and account early
docs.text:
1. On Windows, open Settings > Time & language > Date & time and turn on Set time automatically. Choose 6 · Check UTC clock in NameMCSniper and check that the sources agree. Read the estimated UTC uncertainty alongside the offset. Microsoft's Windows time settings guide
  2. Use 2 · Check my Minecraft account or 7 · Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt) to confirm the Java profile UUID and rename eligibility. For a future run, NameMCSniper checks eligibility again shortly before dispatch. Minecraft allows one Java profile name change every 30 days. Authentication · Minecraft Help
  3. Use a stable connection and keep the machine awake until the outcome appears. If the clock check fails, resolve it while there is still time to preview the schedule again. Clock troubleshooting

docs.title: Read the timing numbers
docs.text:
Choose 5 · Measure dispatch timing or run namemcsniper benchmark --samples 100. It runs the scheduler offline against scripted responses and reports the median, 95th percentile, and worst dispatch delay, plus missed slots. Run it on the machine you plan to use under its usual load.

Measurement What it measures Benchmark dispatch delay How late the local scheduler starts a scripted request relative to its slot. UTC offset and estimated uncertainty How far the system clock appears to be from UTC and how uncertain the app's correction is. Clock check round trip The round trip to a public NTP server. The elapsed time reported for a live attempt covers work with Minecraft Services, including any follow-up profile check.

An offline benchmark cannot tell you when Minecraft will process a request or when the name will actually drop. Start with the default single attempt and stop if Minecraft returns HTTP 429. Follow Retry-After when the response provides it. MCsniperGO's maintainers reported that rate limits made automated claims ineffective in their testing. MCsniperGO maintainer notice

docs.title: Launching the app
docs.text: On Windows, open namemcsniper.exe to start the menu. If PowerShell says the command is unknown, open a terminal in the folder that contains the executable and run .\namemcsniper.exe. You can also use its full path. Installation

docs.title: The token or proxy list is missing
docs.text:
If a list is missing, the menu shows the expected path. Copy tokens.txt.example or proxies.txt.example into the displayed folder, remove .example from the copy’s name, and add one entry per line. If you create the file in Windows Notepad, choose Save as type > All files to avoid a filename such as tokens.txt.txt. Keep credential files private.

Menu options 7 · Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt) and 4 · Test proxies show the default path before reading it. They look in the working folder first and then beside the executable. Press Enter to use the displayed path, or paste the full path to another file. The check-tokens command uses the same search order when you omit the path. The test-proxies command defaults to the working folder. Pass a file path to use a different list. Token file format · Proxy file format

.\namemcsniper.exe check-tokens 'C:\Path To Files\tokens.txt'
.\namemcsniper.exe test-proxies 'C:\Path To Files\proxies.txt'

docs.title: Account checks
docs.text:
• Invalid or expired token. Get a fresh Minecraft Services bearer token from your own signed-in Minecraft session, then use 2 · Check my Minecraft account to verify it. Use the hidden prompt for a single token. Authentication
  • Java profile missing or UUID mismatch. Check that the signed-in account has an existing Java Edition profile. Use the Java profile UUID returned by the checker when specifying --account. Minecraft Help
  • Profile cannot change its name yet. Wait until Minecraft reports it can rename. The Java Edition rename cooldown is 30 days. A token can be valid while the profile is on cooldown. Minecraft Help

docs.title: Drop estimates and times
docs.text:
• 3NAME gives no usable estimate. The automatic lookup covers three-character names. If the estimate is missing, expired, or too wide for automatic scheduling, use a future time you can verify. 3NAME
  • The timestamp is rejected. Include Z or a numeric offset, as in 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z or 2030-06-01T14:00:00.250-04:00. The CLI also accepts Unix milliseconds. An automatic 3NAME window or an explicit --at and --until range must fit within 30 seconds. Schedule options
  • The schedule ends without sending. Check the log for a skipped slot or a failed account check. If the machine was asleep or busy when the slot arrived, the one-second grace period may have elapsed. Review the time and choose a valid future slot.

docs.title: Clock checks
docs.text:
• Could not get an agreed UTC offset. Choose 6 · Check UTC clock again on a stable connection. The app needs replies from two public NTP sources that agree within 50 ms. If the failure persists, check whether the network or firewall permits outbound UDP port 123. If it is a managed network, use a network that allows NTP. NTP specification
  • Offset exceeds five minutes. On Windows, open Settings > Time & language > Date & time and enable Set time automatically. Use Sync now if available, then run the app's check again. Verify the system date and time if the offset persists. Microsoft's Windows time settings guide
  • Estimated uncertainty is too high or the clock changed. Check the network and keep the computer awake. Let the system time settle after a manual change, then run 6 · Check UTC clock. An absolute live run stops if it cannot verify UTC. Restart with a verified clock and a future time. How clock verification works

docs.title: Proxy tests
docs.text: Check that each entry uses a supported HTTP or HTTPS proxy format. healthy (HTTP 401) means the unauthenticated HTTPS probe reached Minecraft Services and received the expected response. If exporting fails, use a new filename because the checker requires a new output file. Exported entries retain credentials. Proxy setup

docs.title: Live outcomes
docs.text:
• HTTP 429 or exit code 3. Minecraft Services rate limited an account check or rename request. A rate limit during preflight stops the run before dispatch. If the app displays Retry-After, wait at least that long before trying again.
  • Outcome uncertain or exit code 4. Run namemcsniper check and look at the current profile name. For a group run, use the outcome shown for each profile to decide which accounts to check. Do the same after cancelling during a request. Minecraft may have processed the rename before the reply was lost.
  • Name still unavailable. Compare the dispatched UTC time with the drop estimate. The estimate can differ from the actual release, and another player may have claimed the name.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
Each live run prints its log path. On Windows, open %LOCALAPPDATA%\NameMCSniper\logs in File Explorer. On macOS, look under ~/Library/Logs/NameMCSniper. On Linux, look under $XDG_STATE_HOME/namemcsniper/logs or ~/.local/state/namemcsniper/logs when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset.

If you ask for help, include the app version from namemcsniper --version, your operating system, and the relevant error or log lines. Redact profile details you want to keep private and keep bearer tokens and proxy credentials out of the report. Support

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Account checks and live renames use a Minecraft Services bearer token for an existing Java Edition profile. Treat the token like a password and keep it in a private file, a secret manager, or the app's hidden prompt.

docs.title: Find a token from your own session
docs.text:
1. Sign in to Minecraft My Games and open your browser's developer tools to the Network panel.
  2. Under Minecraft: Java Edition, select Change Profile Name to open the form. Leave the form open without submitting a rename.
  3. Find the GET /minecraft/profile/namechange request to api.minecraftservices.com. Under Request Headers, look for Authorization. If it contains Bearer …, copy the token after Bearer.
  4. In NameMCSniper, choose 2 · Check my Minecraft account and paste at the hidden prompt. Review the Java profile name, UUID, and rename eligibility.

Minecraft allows one Java profile name change every 30 days. A token can pass the account check while the profile is still on cooldown. Minecraft Help

docs.title: Check a list
docs.text:
Create a private tokens.txt beside the executable, with one token per line and an optional Bearer prefix. The checker accepts up to 64 entries, ignoring blank lines and lines beginning with #.

Choose 7 · Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt) and accept the displayed file path or supply your own. The report shows line numbers and profile eligibility. For a shell, use namemcsniper check-tokens FILE. Omitting FILE checks for tokens.txt in the working directory first, then beside the executable.

docs.title: Use a token for a live rename
docs.text:
In the menu, paste one token or choose Use all eligible profiles from tokens.txt. Review the target, time, and profiles before typing RENAME. In scripts, use --live --tokens-file FILE to select every distinct eligible profile, or add --account flags to select specific UUIDs from the list. For a single profile, you can pass --live --account UUID and supply its token at the hidden prompt, from NAMEMCSNIPER_TOKEN, or from standard input with --token-stdin. Command reference

Use a fresh token that will still be valid at preflight. If Minecraft returns HTTP 401, get a fresh token and check the account again. If the profile check fails, confirm the signed-in account has an existing Java Edition profile.

docs.title: Local files and settings
docs.text:
Set the target, timing, and account from the guided menu or with command-line flags. Keep optional token and proxy lists in plain UTF-8 text files.

File Contents Menu action tokens.txt One Minecraft Services bearer token per line 7 · Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt), or Use all eligible profiles from tokens.txt during live setup proxies.txt One HTTP or HTTPS proxy per line 4 · Test proxies proxies_working.txt Passing entries from a proxy test, including any credentials Optional export from 4 · Test proxies

docs.title: Where to put the lists
docs.text:
Create tokens.txt or proxies.txt in the folder with namemcsniper.exe if you need one. The menu shows the default path and accepts another path. It looks in the working directory first, then beside the executable. When you omit the file argument, check-tokens uses the same search order and test-proxies looks only in the working directory.

Both input lists accept blank lines and comments that start with #. Keep lists containing credentials out of version control and screenshots. See Authentication and Proxy setup for formats and limits.

docs.title: Set the time
docs.text: Use a 3NAME estimate for a three-character name, pick Two minutes from now in the guided menu, or enter an absolute time. Absolute inputs accept RFC 3339 with a time zone offset, such as 2030-06-01T14:00:00.250-04:00, or Unix milliseconds. Replace the example with your chosen time. Scheduling a rename

docs.title: Open a Windows build
docs.text:
Double-click the namemcsniper.exe supplied with your Rust build to open the guided terminal menu. Choose 3 · Try an offline simulation to test it without signing in to Minecraft.

If you use PowerShell, open it in the folder containing the executable.

.\namemcsniper.exe --help
.\namemcsniper.exe simulate

docs.title: Build from source
docs.text:
Use the NameMCSniper Rust checkout containing Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock. Install stable Rust with rustup and follow its prompts for the Visual Studio C++ build tools on Windows. Rust installation guide

On Debian or Ubuntu, install pkg-config and libssl-dev before building.

From the Rust checkout, build the executable.

cargo build --locked --release

On Windows, open target\release\namemcsniper.exe. On Linux or macOS, run the executable from the checkout.

./target/release/namemcsniper

To install namemcsniper on your command path, run cargo install --locked --path . from the Rust checkout.

docs.title: First run
docs.text: Start with the simulation, then use the guided menu to look up a name or preview a schedule. Set up authentication when you want to check an account or prepare a live rename.

docs.title: Live account changes
docs.text:
Use live functionality only on profiles you are authorized to rename. Follow the applicable Minecraft, Microsoft, and network provider terms and respect service rate limits.

The guided menu displays the profiles, target, and time before asking you to type RENAME. A scripted live run requires --live and an explicit profile or token file. Live workflow

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text: Treat bearer tokens like passwords. Keep token lists and authenticated proxy files private, including any working proxy list you export. Redact credentials before sharing logs, command output, or screenshots.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Use Troubleshooting to narrow down an account, timing, or connection problem.

docs.title: Reproduce the issue
docs.text:
Run these from a terminal where namemcsniper is available. On Windows, you can also open the executable and use the corresponding menu options.

namemcsniper --version
namemcsniper simulate
namemcsniper benchmark --samples 100

For an account problem, use namemcsniper check or namemcsniper check-tokens FILE. For a timing problem, use namemcsniper clock-check. Command reference

docs.title: Report a bug
docs.text:
Search for an existing report before opening a new one. Include the app version, operating system, the menu steps or command, and what happened. If you built from source, include the revision. NameMCSniper issues

Use the log path printed by a live run to find the relevant excerpt. Redact bearer tokens, proxy credentials, and any private profile details before sharing output or screenshots. Report credential leaks and vulnerabilities privately to the maintainers. Repository owner

docs.title: Schedule a rename
docs.text:
Launch the Rust executable with no arguments to open the menu. On Windows, open namemcsniper.exe or run it in PowerShell.

.\namemcsniper.exe

docs.title: Practice with the menu
docs.text: Menu choice What it does 1. Schedule a name change Choose a target and time, then review an offline preview before deciding whether to go live. 2. Check my Minecraft account Check one Minecraft Services bearer token and view the Java profile and rename eligibility. 3. Try an offline simulation Rehearse a name change without an account or a live request. 4. Test proxies Check HTTPS reachability through the entries in your proxy list. 5. Measure dispatch timing Measure how close your computer gets to its scheduled dispatch times in an offline test. 6. Check UTC clock Check whether the app can verify UTC using public time sources. 7. Test bearer tokens (tokens.txt) Check multiple bearer tokens and see which Java profiles are eligible. 0. Exit Close the app.

docs.title: Schedule a live name change
docs.text:
1. Choose Schedule a name change and enter the target username.
  2. Choose Two minutes from now, Enter a time, or an available Use 3NAME Latest or Use 3NAME Earliest option. For a manual time, use a timestamp with a UTC offset, such as 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z, or Unix milliseconds.
  3. Read the offline preview. Choose Continue to live setup when the target and time are correct.
  4. Choose Paste one token or Use all eligible profiles from tokens.txt. For a list, accept the displayed path or enter your own. The app selects every distinct eligible Java profile from up to 64 token entries and skips profiles that already hold the target name. Create a token list.
  5. Review the target, scheduled time, current names, and UUIDs. Type RENAME to confirm or press Enter to cancel.

The menu schedules one slot. For a group, the app sends one concurrent name-change request per profile that passes the final check. The app schedules those checks 20 seconds before the slot for one to four profiles, and up to 2 minutes 45 seconds before the slot for 64 profiles. If you finish setup after that point, checks start as soon as possible.

docs.title: Pick a time from 3NAME
docs.text:
For a three-character username, the menu looks up the 3NAME window and offers any usable future endpoint of the range. The range is an estimate. Use 3NAME Latest schedules one attempt at the later time, and Use 3NAME Earliest schedules one at the earlier time. If no suitable lookup time is available, choose Enter a time and use a timestamp you have verified.

Run drop NAME to inspect the lookup separately. Absolute live schedules, including 3NAME and manual timestamps, require a verified UTC clock. Two minutes from now measures elapsed time from when you choose it. Timing and preparation.

docs.title: Run logs
docs.text:
A live run prints its log path when the file opens. Use the log to check the selected profiles, dispatch timing, and results. The app keeps bearer tokens out of the log.

Platform Default log directory Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\NameMCSniper\logs macOS ~/Library/Logs/NameMCSniper Linux $XDG_STATE_HOME/namemcsniper/logs or ~/.local/state/namemcsniper/logs

If the result is uncertain, check the final log result and the affected Minecraft profile before another live run.

For terminal flags and exit codes, see the command reference.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
Launch namemcsniper with no arguments in a terminal for the guided menu. The examples use the executable name on your PATH. In PowerShell, use .\namemcsniper.exe if you are running it from the current folder. Installation.

Command Behavior menu Opens the guided menu. check [--token-stdin] Checks one Minecraft Services bearer token, Java profile, and rename eligibility. Prompts for the token if needed. check-tokens [FILE] Checks tokens from a file and reports each result by line. With no path, looks for tokens.txt in the current folder first, then beside the executable. test-proxies [FILE] [--output FILE] Tests a proxy list and optionally writes passing entries to a new file. Defaults to proxies.txt in the current folder. drop NAME [--at TIME] [--until TIME] Looks up a three-character name on 3NAME or displays the time or range you entered. snipe NAME [OPTIONS] Previews a schedule. To go live, add --live and specify a profile or token file. simulate [--scenario SCENARIO] Runs an offline simulation. Scenarios are success, unavailable, rate-limited, uncertain, and rejected. Defaults to success. benchmark [--samples N] Measures local dispatch delay offline. Supports 1 to 200 samples and defaults to 40. clock-check Checks UTC against public time sources. --help Lists commands. Add it after a command to see that command’s options. --version Prints the version of the executable.

The Rust CLI also recognizes the aliases check-accounts for check, test-tokens for check-tokens, and snipe-at for snipe.

docs.title: Look up or preview a time
docs.text:
namemcsniper drop abc
namemcsniper snipe ExampleName
namemcsniper snipe ExampleName --at 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z
namemcsniper snipe ExampleName --at 2030-06-01T18:00:00Z --until 2030-06-01T18:00:20Z --attempts 3

drop NAME looks up 3NAME for names made of exactly three letters, digits, or underscores. A lookup may return a wide range or only a latest time. An offline snipe NAME without --at previews an example time two seconds in the future. Add --at to preview a timestamp you supply.

docs.title: Schedule a live change
docs.text:
Run check or check-tokens first to find your Java UUID and confirm rename eligibility. Replace UUID, FIRST_UUID, and SECOND_UUID in the examples with the UUIDs you select. Use accounts you control. Authentication.

namemcsniper snipe ExampleName --at 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z --live --account UUID
namemcsniper snipe ExampleName --at 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z --live --tokens-file tokens.txt
namemcsniper snipe ExampleName --at 2030-06-01T18:00:00.250Z --live --account FIRST_UUID --account SECOND_UUID --tokens-file tokens.txt
Flag Behavior --at TIME Sets the first time of an exact schedule or the earliest time of a bounded schedule. Use RFC 3339 with Z or an explicit offset, or Unix milliseconds. --until TIME Sets the latest time of a range. Requires --at. For scheduling, the range can be at most 30 seconds wide. --attempts N Defaults to 1. Selecting exactly one profile with --account allows up to 3 slots. --interval SECONDS Sets the minimum spacing between slots. Defaults to 10 seconds and supports 10 to 30. --live Enables live requests and requires --account UUID or --tokens-file FILE. --account UUID Selects a Java profile and requires --live. Repeat with --tokens-file to select up to 64 distinct profiles. --tokens-file FILE Loads up to 64 token entries and requires --live. Without --account, selects every distinct eligible profile and skips profiles that already hold the target name. --token-stdin Reads a single bearer token from the first line of standard input. Requires --live for snipe and is mutually exclusive with --tokens-file.

A single-account run can read the token from a hidden prompt or NAMEMCSNIPER_TOKEN when neither token flag is set. A token-file run with no UUIDs or with multiple UUIDs requires the default one slot. The app dispatches one concurrent request per ready profile at that slot.

A live run without --at looks up 3NAME for a three-character target and needs a usable window of at most 30 seconds. All absolute live schedules require a verified UTC clock. A bounded schedule with one slot uses the latest time. If you request more slots, the app spaces them within the range and uses fewer when the interval leaves insufficient room. An exact schedule starts at --at and spaces later slots by the interval.

With exactly one --account, a scheduled retry is possible only after the service confirms the name is unavailable. A rate limit or uncertain result stops further attempts. Timing and preparation.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Completed successfully. A group can return success when one profile confirmed a name change. 1 A command failed. For check-tokens, one or more token checks failed. 2 Invalid command-line arguments. 3 Minecraft Services rate limited a single-account check, a token-list check, or live preflight. This code also applies when rate limiting is the final rename outcome. 4 The live name-change outcome was uncertain. Check the run log and profile. 130 Live run interrupted with Ctrl+C. If a request was in flight, check the selected profiles before trying again.

The app displays the Retry-After wait when Minecraft Services supplies one. A rate limit during preflight stops the run before dispatch.

docs.title: Discord setup
docs.text: The Discord webhook setup applied to the Python edition. The Rust rebuild shows countdowns and results in the terminal and saves live run details locally. Find your run log.

docs.title: Test a proxy list
docs.text: The proxy tester checks whether an HTTP or HTTPS proxy can reach Minecraft Services over HTTPS. Live name changes and account checks use a direct connection.

docs.title: Create the list
docs.text:
Create a UTF-8 file called proxies.txt and add one proxy per line. The app accepts an HTTP or HTTPS URL, a bare host:port, or the provider format host:port@username:password. Both forms without a scheme use HTTP. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

# Replace these example entries with your own
proxy.example:8080
https://proxy.example:8443
http://username:example-password@proxy.example:8080
proxy.example:8080@username:example-password

Percent-encode reserved characters in the username or password. For example, write %40 for an @ in a password. The list supports up to 256 entries and 64 KiB.

docs.title: Run the check
docs.text:
In the menu, choose Test proxies. The default is proxies.txt in the current folder if it exists, then proxies.txt beside the executable. Press Enter to use the displayed path or enter a path to your list. Choose 1 to save passing entries to proxies_working.txt next to the input file. Press Enter or 0 to test without exporting, or enter a different output filename.

From a shell, run one of these commands.

namemcsniper test-proxies
namemcsniper test-proxies proxies.txt --output proxies_working.txt

The shell command looks in the current folder when you omit the input filename. Choose a new file for the export. It keeps the original entries, including credentials, so keep the exported list private.

docs.title: Read the results
docs.text:
The tester sends an unauthenticated HTTPS profile request through each proxy. The expected 401 Unauthorized response passes the reachability check. The terminal shows redacted addresses and elapsed time for each result.

To schedule a name change, follow the menu guide.
